shipped_rows.title_o: Assessment protocol for identifying preferred social consequences
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: Token systems had reinforcing value similar to primary reinforcers for 2 of the 4 learners, but resulted in lower rates of responding than primary reinforcers for the other 2 learners. Differentiated responding across learners may warrant variation in clinical recommendations on the use of tokens. The results of this study support formal assessment of token system effectiveness, and the MSA procedure provides an efficient method by which to conduct such assessments.

prior_scientific_decisions.quote: The current research sought to systematically replicate Smaby et al. (2007) and Cividini-Motta and Ahearn’s (2013) use of the MSA, speci ﬁ cally to evaluate the relative reinforcing ef ﬁ cacy of the individual components of a token economy in a brief assessment.
prior_scientific_decisions.reason: The authors explicitly state that they replicated Smaby et al.'s (2007) use of the multiple-schedule reinforcer assessment (MSA) procedure in a new application evaluating token economy components, and only note the general viability of the method rather than comparing against a specific empirical finding of Smaby et al. (2007). Shipped's 'mixed' misinterprets heterogeneous responder profiles across the four learners in the new sample as a replication comparison.
